Acomys cahirinus.thesis: Acomys cahirinus is a strong mammalian regeneration flagship because scar-free repair is repeatedly observed across tissues and is associated with a coordinated extracellular-matrix plus immune-state program. IL10 is treated only as a translational anchor, not as a sufficient causal explanation.
Acomys cahirinus.external_validation_question: Does the published Acomys evidence justify a pre-registered causal experiment testing a coordinated ECM/immune regeneration program, rather than a single anti-inflammatory mechanism, and which perturbation would most efficiently falsify that thesis?

human_bridge.animal_anchor: Acomys cahirinus IL10 / regenerative immune context
human_bridge.boundary: The platform has previously resolved an Acomys-to-human IL10 provider chain, but this package does not treat that as proof that IL10 causes regeneration or fibrosis reversal in humans.

literature_evidence.title: Perfect chronic skeletal muscle regeneration in adult spiny mice, Acomys cahirinus
literature_evidence.supports: Repeated adult mammalian skeletal-muscle regeneration with reduced inflammatory/fibrotic signatures.

literature_evidence.title: Comparative transcriptomic analysis of dermal wound healing reveals de novo skeletal muscle regeneration in Acomys cahirinus
literature_evidence.supports: De novo skeletal-muscle regeneration; differential ECM, Wnt and immune programs; higher Il10 expression.

literature_evidence.title: Complex Tissue Regeneration in Mammals Is Associated With Reduced Inflammatory Cytokines and an Influx of T Cells
literature_evidence.supports: Regeneration differs from fibrotic repair in immune-state composition; COX-2 suppression alone was insufficient, arguing against a simplistic anti-inflammatory explanation.

literature_evidence.title: ECM-Focused Proteomic Analysis of Ear Punch Regeneration in Acomys cahirinus
literature_evidence.supports: Proteomic evidence that extracellular-matrix composition differs during regenerative versus fibrotic repair.

literature_evidence.title: Acomys cahirinus develop lung stroma distortion but not fibrosis after bleomycin-induced injury
literature_evidence.supports: Independent recent organ-level evidence consistent with an unusual anti-fibrotic injury response.

proposed_falsification.hypothesis: A coordinated ECM/immune state is required for the Acomys regenerative phenotype; manipulating one anti-inflammatory node alone will not reproduce the full phenotype.
minimum_test: Define a matched Acomys-versus-Mus wound model and pre-register outcome metrics.
Perturb a candidate immune anchor and an ECM/remodeling anchor separately and jointly.
Measure regeneration, fibrosis, ECM composition and immune-cell/cytokine state.
Require the joint model to outperform single-node explanations under pre-registered criteria.
kill_criteria: A single-node perturbation fully explains the regenerative phenotype.
The proposed combined signature fails to reproduce across independent Acomys datasets.
The effect disappears under matched injury/timepoint controls.

Somniosus microcephalus.thesis: Greenland shark longevity is a promising comparative-genomics program, but the currently curated evidence package is less experimentally direct than Acomys regeneration.
Somniosus microcephalus.external_validation_question: Which Greenland-shark longevity mechanism has the strongest causal evidence suitable for direct experimental falsification?

literature_evidence.title: Potential factors contributing to extreme longevity in the Greenland shark
literature_evidence.supports: Current synthesis of candidate longevity mechanisms including genome-maintenance pathways.
